requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale:
The requirement is met: I found no gap in the code or the tests. I read the two `{impl}` items and the lib.rs helpers they call. I read the tests as shown in the inputs and did not run them.

**Implementation**
- `src/fenced.rs#fn[markdown_fences]` leaves colon-fenced references literal when they sit inside code or raw HTML. It calls `protected_ranges`, which collects `Tag::CodeBlock`, `Event::Code`, `Event::Html` and `Event::InlineHtml` ranges from the Markdown parser. That covers inline code, fenced code, HTML blocks, HTML comments, and inline tags including their attributes. Text between inline tags is not in any of those ranges, so it stays ordinary Markdown.
- `src/terms.rs#fn[direct_references]` calls `referenced_terms`, which calls `reference_roles` in lib.rs.
  - `reference_roles` skips escaped roles through `is_escaped` and skips protected ranges, so escaped roles and role-looking text in code or raw HTML stay literal.
  - With `markdown` false, nothing is protected, which matches the plain-text behaviour the tests expect.
- `direct_references` also reaches `definition_blocks` in lib.rs.
  - `definition_blocks` only matches colon-fence directives and skips any whose opening line overlaps `code_block_ranges`. A `:::{req}` inside a fenced code example therefore defines nothing.
  - A legacy inline `{req}` role never matches a colon fence, so it defines nothing either.
- Because `reference_roles`, `protected_ranges` and `definition_blocks` are reachable from the two `{impl}` items, none of them needs its own reference. Their callers (`text_references`, `file_references`, `replace_inline_references`) only call this logic.

**Tests**
- Escaped roles, inline code, fenced code and raw HTML are tested in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal]`, which includes the escaped-backslash case.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal]` covers raw HTML. It checks an HTML block, an HTML comment, an inline comment, tag attributes, and a role between inline tags that does count.
- `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_in_raw_html_stay_literal]` covers fences in HTML blocks, HTML comments and tag attributes.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal]` checks `.md`, `.markdown`, `.MD` and `.Markdown` files against a plain `.txt` file.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs]` also carries a `{test}` reference to this requirement.
- A `{req}` fence inside a fenced code example and a legacy `{req}` role are tested in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal]` and `fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown]` checks that requirement bodies are scanned as Markdown, so a fenced example inside one stays literal.
- For `{term}` roles, `src/terms.rs#mod[tests]/fn[term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles]` and `tests/definitions.rs#fn[literal_term_roles_in_subject_and_requirements_inputs_need_no_definition]` test the same literal cases. The second also checks that the same role written as a real reference is still counted.

All tests carry `{test}` references to the requirement. I found no unspecified behaviour and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.
